lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Look and write

details: Look and write serves as a comprehensive review of the unit. Students integrate vocabulary and grammar to write complete sentences describing the pictures, consolidating all learning points.
Look for correct identification of subjects and activities, accurate spelling, and correct use of third-person grammar in the completed sentences.
“Wow, it is tricky keeping track of who has which class when! Can you help me fill in these gaps so I can make everyone a timetable?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Listen and tick

details: Listen and tick assesses students’ listening comprehension of the unit's key language. Students listen for specific details about timetables and activities, then tick the correct box to show understanding.
Look for focused listening and the ability to identify key information, demonstrated by accurately ticking the correct boxes for each item.
“Now for a listening challenge so we can complete our timetables.. I need you to use your expert ears to help me. Listen carefully and tick the correct boxes!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - A Look and write

details: Look and write consolidates the unit's vocabulary in a timetable format. Students use the picture clues to complete the chart, writing the correct subjects and class activities.
Look for accurate analysis of the picture clues and correct ticking of the boxes that form a logical question and answer pair.
“Oh dear, I thought our timetables were complete but this one has gaps! Look at the pictures carefully and write in the missing subjects and activities.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Speaking Our Silly Classes!

details: Our Silly Classes is a culminating speaking game that encourages fluency and creative use of language. Students generate random sentences and use critical thinking to identify the ‘silly’ combinations.
Look for active participation, spontaneous sentence production, correct identification of silly sentences, and enthusiastic interaction within the groups.
“Phew - everyone has a timetable now. But are they right? Spin the wheel to find out!”
